definitions.explanation: Describes a flavor that combines sweetness and sourness, like certain fruits or sauces.
Describes a nostalgic or sentimental feeling that combines happiness and sadness, often associated with youthful memories.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{苺|いちご}→苺：01028_ichigo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{甘酸|あまず}っぱくて⟦おいしい→おいしい：00740_oishii⟧。
examples.english: These strawberries are sweet and sour and delicious.

examples.japanese: {甘酸|あまず}っぱい⟦ソース→ソース：17673_soosu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{鶏肉|とりにく}→鶏肉：02919_toriniku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I ate chicken with sweet and sour sauce.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦みかん→みかん：01036_mikan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{甘酸|あまず}っぱくて⟦{美味|おい}しい→おいしい：00740_oishii⟧。
examples.english: This mandarin orange is sweet and sour and delicious.

examples.japanese: {甘酸|あまず}っぱい⟦{青春|せいしゅん}→青春：14613_seishun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{思|おも}い{出|で}→思い出：00331_omoide⟧。
⟦{初恋|はつこい}→初恋：17445_hatsukoi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{甘酸|あまず}っぱい⟦{記憶|きおく}→記憶：00234_kioku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{蘇|よみがえ}った→蘇る：04004_yomigaeru⟧。
examples.english: The bittersweet memories of my first love came back.

examples.japanese: ⟦{卒業式|そつぎょうしき}→卒業式：05584_sotsugyoushiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{写真|しゃしん}→写真：00753_shashin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}ると→見る：00283_miru⟧、{甘酸|あまず}っぱい⟦{気持|きも}ち→気持ち：01385_kimochi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: When I look at graduation photos, I get a bittersweet feeling.

notes:
{甘酸|あまず}っぱい is an i-adjective combining ⟦{甘|あま}い→甘い：00617_amai⟧ (sweet) and ⟦{酸|す}っぱい→酸っぱい：02346_suppai⟧ (sour). It has both a literal taste meaning and a figurative emotional meaning.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {甘酸|あまず}っぱく
- Past: {甘酸|あまず}っぱかった

TASTE USAGE:
- {甘酸|あまず}っぱい⟦ソース→ソース：17673_soosu⟧: sweet and sour sauce
- {甘酸|あまず}っぱい⟦{果物|くだもの}→果物：00509_kudamono⟧: sweet and sour fruit
- Common with berries, citrus, and vinegar-based dishes

EMOTIONAL USAGE:
Describes bittersweet or nostalgic feelings, especially related to:
- ⟦{青春|せいしゅん}→青春：14613_seishun⟧: youth
- ⟦{初恋|はつこい}→初恋：17445_hatsukoi⟧: first love
- ⟦{思|おも}い{出|で}→思い出：00331_omoide⟧: memories

This figurative usage is very common in literature and everyday conversation. The emotional sense evokes a mix of fondness and wistfulness.
